summary: Hosted API: customer experiencing timeouts under high load (suspected allocator pressure / KV cache fragmentation)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports intermittent request timeouts (client-side 30s) when sending bursts of chat completions through Hosted API.
- Pattern: stable when sustained at ~40 RPS, but timeouts spike during short bursts (~120–160 RPS) with mixed prompt sizes.
- Customer asks for immediate mitigation guidance while we investigate.

Customer impact
- End-user experience: elevated timeout rate during peak ingestion windows.
- Business impact: customer temporarily disabled a feature flag that drives LLM usage during peak hours.

Environment / context
- Product: Hosted API
- Region: us-east
- Models: rw-chat-70b and rw-chat-34b (customer alternates by route)
- Traffic pattern: bursty, mixed context lengths (small + occasional long-context requests)
- Customer client timeout: 30s; retry: none (at time of report)

What we observed (Support/SRE)
- Correlates with p99 latency spikes and increased 504s at the API gateway.
- Runtime telemetry showed elevated allocation pressure signals and an increase in KV cache eviction churn during bursts (consistent with the known issue: KV cache fragmentation under bursts).
- No evidence of a single-tenant quota/429 problem; this appears to be pool-level tail latency.

Ask
- Provide customer-facing mitigations (safe configuration changes on client + server-side routing recommendations).
- Confirm whether incident is ongoing and whether a rollback / pool routing action is required.

References
- Runbook: Mitigating KV cache fragmentation incidents
- Known issue: KV cache fragmentation under bursts
- Related workstream: KV cache compaction improvements (runtime feature flag; not yet broadly enabled)
comments: 2025-02-18 08:12 PT — Aisha Bello (Support): Customer (Hearthside Analytics) reporting timeouts via Hosted API in us-east. They see bursts where ~10–15% of requests exceed 30s and fail. Asking for immediate mitigation guidance. Attaching customer-provided note: “No 429s; responses just hang then timeout.”

2025-02-18 08:18 PT — Aisha Bello (Support): Requested from customer: request IDs (x-rw-request-id), timestamps, model/route used, max_tokens, and whether streaming is enabled. Also asked whether they can temporarily cap concurrency on their side.

2025-02-18 08:31 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE): Looking at us-east hosted pool. There is a coincident rise in p99 decode latency and gateway 504s in the last hour. Not seeing infra errors (GPU node health OK). Allocator pressure signal elevated; eviction rate spiky. This resembles the recent fragmentation-under-bursts pattern (see Confluence runbook).

2025-02-18 08:38 PT — Sean Gallagher (SRE): +1. Fragmentation signal is elevated in one of the shared pools that serves rw-chat-70b. No hard OOMs, but allocator failures are close to threshold; admission control gets more aggressive -> tail spikes. Suggest we apply interim tuning from the runbook rather than paging runtime immediately, unless it persists >30 min.

2025-02-18 08:44 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE): Immediate mitigations we can recommend (customer-safe): (1) enable retries with jittered backoff for 504/timeouts; (2) cap client-side concurrency (max in-flight) during burst windows; (3) reduce max_tokens where possible; (4) avoid mixing long-context requests on the same route during bursts (split into two routes if they can) so scheduler doesn’t oscillate.

SRE-side mitigations (we can do): temporarily route their traffic to a less-congested pool / alternate region if available, and tighten admission parameters to reduce thrash. Will validate current headroom first.

2025-02-18 09:03 PT — Aisha Bello (Support): Customer provided 12 request IDs between 07:50–08:05 PT; most were rw-chat-70b, max_tokens=1024, streaming disabled. They confirmed burst windows from their ETL: 10-minute peaks at the top of the hour. Client timeout fixed at 30s; no retries today.

2025-02-18 09:15 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE): Checked the request IDs; they align with p99 spikes and elevated eviction churn. Not a single bad host. This is pool behavior under burst + mixed seq lengths. Applying runbook step: shift 20% of rw-chat-70b traffic from hosted pool use1-a to use1-c for 2 hours; also increasing scheduler backpressure sensitivity to reduce allocator thrash (no customer-visible config change required). Monitoring.

2025-02-18 09:42 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE): Post-change: gateway 504s down; p99 improving. Allocation failures near zero. Still some tail spikes when long-context requests arrive during bursts, but materially better.

2025-02-18 10:05 PT — Aisha Bello (Support): Sent mitigations to customer: recommend enabling retries for idempotent requests on 504/timeouts (2–3 attempts, exponential backoff + jitter), cap concurrency during peak bursts, and consider reducing max_tokens or splitting long-context workloads into a separate route/model to avoid mixing during bursts. Also confirmed we applied a server-side routing/tuning mitigation in us-east and are monitoring.

2025-02-19 08:20 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE): 24h check: stable. No further 504 burst events in use1 after routing/tuning. Leaving pool routing as-is until after peak. Linking this to SUP-4422 since long-context traffic appears to exacerbate allocator pressure.

2025-02-20 11:10 PT — Aisha Bello (Support): Customer confirms improvement: timeouts reduced from ~10–15% to <1% during top-of-hour peak; they added retries and reduced concurrency slightly. Closing as Resolved. Follow-up: keep tracking compaction project rollout (feature-flag) for longer-term fix.
resolution:
Resolved via interim operational mitigation and customer-side best practices.

Actions taken
- SRE applied temporary routing shift to a less-congested hosted pool in us-east and tuned backpressure/admission parameters per the “Mitigating KV cache fragmentation incidents” runbook.
- Support provided customer guidance: enable bounded retries with jitter on timeouts/504s, cap client concurrency during bursts, and reduce max_tokens / separate long-context traffic to avoid mixing during burst windows.

Outcome
- Tail latency and gateway 504s decreased; customer reports timeout rate <1% during peak windows.

Follow-ups
- Track/roll in KV cache compaction improvements for a structural reduction in burst tail latencies associated with KV cache fragmentation.
- Ensure fragmentation/allocation metrics retention and labeling are in place (INT-1183 / PR-18423).
